extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent owners, and policymakers interested in PTAB/IPR practice
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and explaining why the PTAB’s all-claims invalidation rate in IPRs is high compared to other USPTO proceedings, and what procedural factors and reforms affect that rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: All-claims invalidation rate
rubrics_metrics.description: The rate at which the PTAB finds all challenged claims invalid (unpatentable), effectively killing off the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the primary outcome metric in the piece. Reported values include ~70% overall for IPRs (55% in 2019 rising to 70% in 2024, 64% through first half FY2025). The author treats large year-to-year variation as an additional concern about process balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross‑proceeding invalidation rate comparison (IPR vs EPR vs inter partes reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare all-claims invalidation rates across different USPTO post-grant proceedings to benchmark PTAB performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited figures: average all-claims invalidation for Ex Parte Reexamination (EPR) ≈ 14%; for inter partes reexamination ≈ 34%; for IPRs ≈ 65–70%. Use caution: USPTO reports EPR data cumulatively back to 1981 and there are reporting errors, so exact EPR figures may be imprecise. The large disparity (IPR much higher) is the puzzle the article analyzes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenger participation (ex parte vs inter partes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the challenger actively participates in the proceeding (inter partes) or not (ex parte) and the resulting effect on outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPRs are ex parte after filing, so the challenger does not participate in re-evaluation; inter partes reexamination and IPRs are inter partes. The article posits challenger participation differences may influence outcomes, potentially explaining some of the differences in invalidation rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and frequency of claim amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: How often patent owners obtain amended claims in the proceeding (motions to amend grant rates / certificates of confirmation including amended claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPR certificates of confirmation included amended claims 63% of the time; inter partes reexamination included amended claims 60% of the time. By contrast, PTAB motions to amend under a pilot had a 24% grant rate (down from an earlier 17%), and patent owners filed motions to amend in only 9% of IPR proceedings (2013–2024). The authors identify the PTAB’s low amendment grant rate as a significant contributor to the elevated all-claims invalidation rate: if more amendments were granted, more motions would be filed and the all-claims invalidation rate would moderate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim construction standard applied in the proceeding (broadest reasonable interpretation vs Phillips standard) and its effect on outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter partes reexamination used the broadest reasonable construction (BRC), which the article notes is more favorable to challengers than the Phillips district court standard used in IPRs from 2018 onwards. The claim construction regime can materially affect invalidity findings and comparability between proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: The evidentiary standard the challenger must meet to prove unpatentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The burden of proof in these proceedings is the preponderance of the evidence and is the same across the compared proceedings, so the authors treat it as not explaining the disparity in invalidation rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudicator competence and approach (APJs vs CRU examiners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Administrative Patent Judges (APJs) adjudicating IPRs are harsher or more diligent than Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors' view: APJs are highly knowledgeable in technology and obviousness law and 'carefully and diligently evaluate' claims against the art; they do not view APJ toughness as the primary explanation for higher IPR invalidation rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness and deference in appellate review (Federal Circuit affirmance rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: How the Federal Circuit reviews and affirms PTAB decisions, including caseload and affirmance percentages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High Federal Circuit affirmance rates for PTAB appeals (≈85–86% reported for 2023–2024) and heavy appellate workload (181 appeals in 2023; 153 in 2024) suggest substantial deference to the PTAB. The authors argue that this deference and appellate capacity constraints may contribute to elevated PTAB invalidation outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of intra‑agency review (PTAB review / Director review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there is an internal agency appellate step before reaching the Federal Circuit and how often Director review is granted for IPRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPRs historically provided a first level of appeal within the agency (PTAB) before Federal Circuit review, offering subject‑matter expert review of examiners' fact findings; the article suggests this likely produces more correct outcomes. For IPRs, Director review is available post‑Arthrex but is granted rarely (~5% of the time) and is not equivalent to a guaranteed internal appellate review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director discretion and institution‑stage reforms (bifurcated institution process, discretionary denial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Director authority to manage institution decisions, including the bifurcation of institution and final merits decisions and discretionary denials considering equitable factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Director Coke Morgan Stewart’s interim processes (March 26, 2025) including a bifurcated institution process and discretionary denials that consider patent owners' 'settled expectations,' absence of earlier challenges, and similar equitable considerations. The authors recommend further use of Director institution authority (including fully reclaiming it and bifurcating institution and merits decision makers) as a reform likely to bring more balance and provide a different decision maker to reassess prior institution determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data reliability and reporting caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations and errors in USPTO statistical reporting that affect interpretation of historical rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO reports EPR statistics cumulatively back to 1981 and the data contains some errors (example: cumulative confirmed certificates reported lower in 2021 than 2020). Analysts should be cautious when relying on raw cumulative figures and should note possible reporting inaccuracies when comparing proceedings.
